title: Billing Disputes and Incorrect Charges
content:
# Billing Disputes and Incorrect Charges

**Article ID:** ART001  
**Category:** Billing  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article explains how to identify, investigate, and resolve billing disputes including duplicate charges, unexpected fees, incorrect plan amounts, and disputed usage charges.

---

## Common Billing Dispute Types

### 1. Duplicate Charges
A duplicate charge occurs when the same service or fee appears more than once in the same billing cycle.

**How to identify:**
- Compare line items in the current bill against the previous month's bill
- Look for two identical amounts with the same description on the same date

**Resolution steps:**
1. Pull up the customer's current and previous bill in the account portal
2. If a duplicate is confirmed, raise a credit note for the duplicate amount
3. Apply the credit to the next invoice automatically
4. Notify the customer by email within 2 business hours

### 2. Wrong Plan Amount Billed
The customer is being billed for a plan that does not match their current active plan.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Verify the active plan in the account system
2. Check if a plan change was made mid-cycle — if so, prorated billing applies
3. If no plan change occurred and the amount is wrong, escalate to Billing Team with account ID and both amounts
4. Issue a credit for the difference if the error is confirmed

### 3. Unexpected Add-on or Service Charge
Customer sees a charge for a feature or add-on they did not request.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Check the account's add-on history for authorisation records
2. If no customer authorisation exists, remove the add-on and reverse the charge
3. If authorisation exists but customer denies it, escalate to the Billing Disputes team

### 4. International / Roaming Charges Disputed
See Article ART004 (International Roaming Charges) for roaming-specific disputes.

---

## Prorated Billing Policy

When a plan changes mid-cycle:
- The customer is charged the old plan rate for days used, plus the new plan rate for remaining days
- Prorated credit or debit appears as a line item on the next bill labelled **"Plan Change Adjustment"**
- This is **not** a billing error

---

## Refund Policy

| Scenario | Refund Timeline |
|---|---|
| Duplicate charge confirmed | Credit applied within 24 hours |
| Wrong plan billed (confirmed) | Credit applied within 48 hours |
| Unauthorised add-on | Credit applied within 24 hours |
| Customer error (authorised) | No refund applicable |

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Billing Team if:
- The disputed amount exceeds ₹2,000
- The customer has disputed the same charge more than twice
- Fraud is suspected (unauthorised account access)
- The account has more than 3 unresolved billing disputes in 6 months

---

## What to Tell the Customer

> *"I've reviewed your bill and can see [finding]. I will [action] and you'll receive a confirmation by email. The credit/correction will appear on your next bill dated [date]."*

Always provide a reference number and timeline. Never promise same-day cash refunds.

title: Broadband Connection Issues — Troubleshooting Guide
content:
# Broadband Connection Issues — Troubleshooting Guide

**Article ID:** ART002  
**Category:** Technical / Connection  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers diagnostic steps and resolutions for broadband connection issues including complete outages, slow speeds, intermittent drops, and Wi-Fi problems.

---

## Step 1 — Quick Triage Questions

Before running diagnostics, establish:
1. Is the issue affecting **all devices** or just one?
2. Is the issue **wired (Ethernet)** or **Wi-Fi** or both?
3. What do the **router lights** show? (Power, Broadband/WAN, Wi-Fi)
4. When did the issue start?
5. Has anything changed recently (new device, router moved, storm)?

---

## Scenario A — Complete Outage (No Internet on Any Device)

### Router Light Status Guide

| Broadband/WAN Light | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Solid Green | Line connected — issue is likely router or device |
| Flashing Green | Syncing — wait 2 minutes |
| Red or Off | Line fault — likely ISP-side issue |

### Resolution Steps

1. **Restart the router:** Unplug power for 60 seconds, plug back in, wait 3 minutes
2. **Check for area outage:** Look up account postcode in the outage tracker (internal tool)
3. **If area outage confirmed:** Inform customer of ETA, log ticket as outage-related, no engineer needed
4. **If no area outage:**
   - Check line signal levels remotely (use diagnostic tool)
   - If signal levels abnormal → schedule engineer visit
   - If signal levels normal → router fault suspected → arrange router replacement

### Common Causes
- Area network outage (check first)
- Loose or damaged cable at junction box
- Router hardware fault
- ISP equipment failure at exchange

---

## Scenario B — Slow Speeds

### Expected Speed Ranges by Plan

| Plan | Expected Download | Minimum Guaranteed |
|---|---|---|
| Fiber 100 | 100 Mbps | 50 Mbps |
| Fiber 500 | 500 Mbps | 250 Mbps |
| Fiber 1000 | 1000 Mbps | 500 Mbps |

**If speed is below minimum guaranteed, the customer is entitled to a remedy under our Speed Guarantee Policy.**

### Diagnosis Steps

1. Ask customer to run speed test at [speedtest.nexusnow.com] on a **wired** connection
2. If wired speed is above minimum → Wi-Fi issue (see Scenario C)
3. If wired speed is below minimum:
   - Check for local congestion (peak hours: 6 PM – 10 PM)
   - Run remote line diagnostics
   - If persistent (3+ days): schedule engineer visit
   - Log fault and apply bill credit if SLA is breached (1 day credit per 5 days below minimum)

---

## Scenario C — Wi-Fi Issues (Wired Works Fine)

**Resolution steps:**
1. Router placement: must be central, elevated, away from microwaves/cordless phones
2. Try changing Wi-Fi channel (auto-select in router settings)
3. If house is large: recommend Wi-Fi extender or mesh upgrade
4. Factory reset router as last resort (warn customer this clears custom settings)

---

## Scenario D — Intermittent Drops

Often caused by:
- Line noise (especially in older copper-fibre hybrid lines)
- Faulty microfilter or socket
- Interference from nearby equipment

**Steps:**
1. Check connection logs in the account portal for drop frequency/pattern
2. If drops are at specific times (e.g., evenings) → likely congestion or line noise
3. If random → run line noise diagnostic
4. Persistent drops → engineer visit required

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Level 2 Technical Support if:
- Issue persists after 2 engineer visits
- Signal levels are normal but outage continues
- Customer reports business-critical impact (working from home, medical device, etc.)
- Customer has been without service for more than 48 hours

---

## SLA and Compensation

| Outage Duration | Compensation |
|---|---|
| Under 24 hours | No automatic compensation |
| 24–48 hours | 1 day bill credit |
| 48–72 hours | 3 days bill credit |
| Over 72 hours | 5 days bill credit + review |

Credits are applied to the next bill automatically once the fault is marked resolved.

title: Plan Changes, Upgrades, and Downgrades
content:
# Plan Changes, Upgrades, and Downgrades

**Article ID:** ART003  
**Category:** Plans & Subscriptions  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers how to handle customer requests to change their broadband or mobile plan — including upgrades, downgrades, bundle changes, and plan comparison queries.

---

## Available Plans Summary

### Broadband Plans

| Plan | Speed | Monthly Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Fiber 100 | 100 Mbps | ₹29.99 |
| Fiber 500 | 500 Mbps | ₹49.99 |
| Fiber 1000 | 1000 Mbps | ₹69.99 |

### Mobile Plans

| Plan | Data | Monthly Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile Basic | 5 GB | ₹9.99 |
| Mobile Plus | 20 GB | ₹19.99 |
| Mobile Max | 100 GB | ₹34.99 |

### Bundle Plans (Broadband + Mobile)

| Plan | Speed | Mobile Data | Monthly Cost | Saving vs Separate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bundle 500 | 500 Mbps | 20 GB | ₹59.99 | ₹9.99/month |
| Bundle Max | 1000 Mbps | 100 GB | ₹89.99 | ₹14.99/month |

---

## Plan Change Rules

### Upgrades
- Effective **immediately** on request
- Customer is charged prorated difference for remaining days in current cycle
- New speed/data limits apply within 2 hours of upgrade

### Downgrades
- Effective from the **next billing date** (not immediate)
- No prorated credit for current cycle
- Customer keeps current plan benefits until end of cycle

### Mid-Contract Changes
- We do not enforce minimum contract periods for residential customers
- Business accounts may have 12-month or 24-month contracts — check before processing

---

## How to Process a Plan Change

1. Confirm the customer's **current plan** and **desired plan**
2. Check account status — suspended accounts cannot change plans
3. Confirm the customer understands:
   - Effective date (immediate for upgrades, next bill date for downgrades)
   - New monthly cost
   - Any prorated charges on next bill
4. Process in the account portal under **Plan Management → Change Plan**
5. Send confirmation email to customer (automated on save)

---

## Bundle Recommendations

Recommend a bundle if:
- Customer has both broadband and mobile with us
- Combined separate plan cost exceeds bundle cost
- Customer asks about saving money

**Talking point:**
> *"I can see you're on Fiber 500 (₹49.99) and Mobile Plus (₹19.99) — that's ₹69.98 per month. Our Bundle 500 gives you the same speeds and data for ₹59.99, saving you ₹9.99 every month."*

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I trial a higher plan and downgrade if I don't like it?**  
A: Yes. Upgrade is immediate. If you downgrade within the same billing cycle, the downgrade takes effect next month — you keep the faster speed until then at no extra cost.

**Q: Will my router need replacing if I upgrade to 1000 Mbps?**  
A: Only if your current router does not support gigabit speeds. Check the router model in the account portal. If a replacement is needed, it will be dispatched within 3 business days at no extra cost.

**Q: Is there a discount for annual payment?**  
A: Annual pre-payment plans offer 10% discount. Available on request — flag to account team.

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Plan Management team if:
- Customer wants a custom plan or pricing not in the standard catalogue
- Customer is on a legacy plan no longer offered — special migration process required
- Business account with contract implications

title: International Roaming — Charges, Activation, and Disputes
content:
# International Roaming — Charges, Activation, and Disputes

**Article ID:** ART004  
**Category:** Mobile / Roaming  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers international roaming charges, how to activate roaming, roaming data packs, and how to handle roaming charge disputes.

---

## Roaming Availability by Plan

| Plan | Roaming Eligible | Roaming Included | Pay-per-use Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile Basic | Yes | No | ₹10/MB data, ₹5/min calls |
| Mobile Plus | Yes | No | ₹8/MB data, ₹4/min calls |
| Mobile Max | Yes | 1 GB included in 30+ countries | ₹5/MB data, ₹3/min calls |
| Bundle plans | Inherits mobile plan rules | — | — |

> **Pay-per-use rates can accumulate very quickly.** Customers should always activate a roaming pack before travelling.

---

## Roaming Packs Available

| Pack Name | Countries | Data | Validity | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Asia Pack | 15 Asian countries | 2 GB | 15 days | ₹599 |
| Gulf Pack | UAE, Saudi, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman | 3 GB | 15 days | ₹799 |
| Europe Pack | 30 European countries | 5 GB | 30 days | ₹1,299 |
| Global Lite | 50+ countries | 1 GB | 10 days | ₹499 |
| Global Max | 80+ countries | 10 GB | 30 days | ₹2,499 |

Packs can be activated via:
- MySelf app → Roaming → Add Pack
- Customer portal → Add-ons → Roaming
- By calling support before departure

---

## How to Activate Roaming

1. Ensure the account is active and in good standing (no overdue balance)
2. Go to account portal → Add-ons → International Roaming → Enable
3. Select a roaming pack if desired
4. Roaming activates within 15 minutes
5. Customer must restart their phone after activation

**Important:** Roaming is disabled by default on all plans to prevent unexpected charges.

---

## Handling Roaming Charge Disputes

### Step 1 — Verify if Roaming Was Active
- Check account portal: Add-ons → Roaming history
- Confirm dates roaming was active vs. dates customer was travelling

### Step 2 — Check if a Pack Was Active
- If a pack was active: charges above the pack allowance are at pay-per-use rates — valid charges
- If no pack was active: all data/calls billed at pay-per-use — likely a surprise to the customer

### Step 3 — Assess Goodwill Adjustment Eligibility

| Scenario | Action |
|---|---|
| Customer was unaware roaming was possible | Apply 25% goodwill adjustment, maximum ₹500 |
| Roaming activated without customer consent | Full reversal of charges |
| Customer travelled without activating pack | Offer post-travel roaming pack at discounted rate (50% off) |
| Charges exceed ₹3,000 in a single trip | Escalate to Billing team for review |

### Step 4 — Educate and Prevent Recurrence
Always explain:
- How to activate a pack before the next trip
- How to set a data usage alert (MySelf app → Alerts → Data)
- That they can temporarily disable roaming from the app

---

## Countries Where Roaming Is Not Available

Roaming is not available in North Korea, Cuba, Iran, Syria, and a small number of restricted territories. If a customer travelled to one of these countries, all data would have been blocked — charges should not appear.

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Billing Team if:
- Roaming charges exceed ₹5,000 in a single cycle
- Customer alleges identity fraud (phone used in another country while customer was in India)
- Account shows roaming usage from two countries simultaneously (possible SIM cloning)

title: Payment Methods, Failed Payments, and Account Suspension
content:
# Payment Methods, Failed Payments, and Account Suspension

**Article ID:** ART005  
**Category:** Billing / Payments  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers accepted payment methods, what happens when a payment fails, the account suspension process, and how to restore a suspended account.

---

## Accepted Payment Methods

| Method | Available | Processing Time |
|---|---|---|
| UPI (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm) | Yes | Instant |
| Debit / Credit Card | Yes | Instant |
| Net Banking | Yes | Up to 2 hours |
| Auto-pay (Standing Instruction) | Yes | On due date |
| Cheque / DD | No | Not accepted |
| Cash | No | Not accepted |

Payments can be made via:
- **MySelf App** → Billing → Pay Now
- **Customer Portal** → Billing → Make Payment
- **IVR** → Call 1800-XXX-XXXX and follow prompts

---

## Failed Payment Process

### Why Payments Fail

- Insufficient funds in bank account
- Card expired or blocked
- UPI daily limit exceeded
- Net banking timeout
- Bank declined (fraud prevention)

### What Happens After a Failed Payment

| Day | Action |
|---|---|
| Day 0 (Due date) | Payment attempt. If fails → SMS + email notification |
| Day 3 | Second automatic retry |
| Day 7 | Final reminder. Account flagged for review |
| Day 14 | Account suspended (services paused) |
| Day 30 | Account marked for cancellation review |
| Day 45 | Account cancelled if payment not received |

---

## Account Suspension

### What Suspension Means
- All internet and mobile services are **paused**
- Incoming calls remain active on mobile (outgoing blocked)
- The customer can still access the customer portal and make payment

### Restoring a Suspended Account

1. Customer pays the outstanding balance in full (or arranges a payment plan — see below)
2. Payment must clear before restoration begins
3. Services typically restore within **1–4 hours** after payment confirmation
4. If services do not restore within 4 hours after payment → escalate to Technical team

### Payment Plans (Instalment Arrangements)

Available to customers with 3+ months of good payment history who are experiencing temporary hardship:

- Maximum 3 monthly instalments for balances up to ₹5,000
- Must be set up before account is suspended (cannot be set up post-suspension)
- One payment plan allowed per 12-month period

To set up: Customer must call support (cannot be done online). Requires agreement to auto-pay.

---

## Reconnection Fees

| Scenario | Fee |
|---|---|
| First suspension in 12 months | No fee |
| Second suspension in 12 months | ₹99 reconnection fee |
| Third or more in 12 months | ₹199 reconnection fee + account review |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: I paid but my service is still not back — what do I do?**  
A: Confirm payment has cleared (check bank statement). If yes, contact support with payment confirmation. Technical team will manually trigger restoration.

**Q: Can I get an extension on my bill due date?**  
A: Due date extensions of up to 7 days are available once per 12-month period. Requires account to be in good standing. Cannot be granted after suspension.

**Q: Will suspension affect my credit score?**  
A: We do not report to credit bureaus. Suspension only affects your service with us.

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Billing Team if:
- Customer claims to have paid but account is still suspended and payment does not appear in system
- Customer requests a payment plan post-suspension
- Balance exceeds ₹10,000 (collections process applies)
- Customer is on a medical dependency plan (priority reconnection required within 2 hours)

title: Account Management — Profile, Security, and Contact Details
content:
# Account Management — Profile, Security, and Contact Details

**Article ID:** ART006  
**Category:** Account Management  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers common account management requests including updating contact details, changing account holder, password resets, SIM management, and account closure.

---

## Updating Contact Details

### Email Address
- Can be changed by the account holder only (security verification required)
- Process: Customer Portal → My Profile → Contact Details → Edit Email
- Verification link sent to **old** email — customer must click to confirm
- If customer no longer has access to old email: must verify by calling support with DOB + account ID

### Phone Number (Mobile Contact)
- Process: Customer Portal → My Profile → Contact Details → Edit Mobile
- OTP sent to the **existing** number to confirm
- If customer has lost the old number: identity verification required (see below)

### Address
- Service address: requires engineer assessment if broadband service is impacted
- Billing address: can be updated directly in portal, effective immediately

---

## Identity Verification Protocol

Used when customers cannot access their registered contact methods:

1. Account ID (required)
2. Full name on account (required)
3. Date of birth (required)
4. Any two of:
   - Last 4 digits of payment card on file
   - Exact amount of last payment
   - Security question answer (if set)

All 4 required fields must match before any account changes are made.

---

## SIM Card Management

### SIM Replacement
- Customer requests new SIM (lost, damaged, or upgrading to eSIM)
- Verify identity first
- New SIM dispatched within 2 business days (standard), same day available at store
- Old SIM is automatically deactivated when new SIM is activated

### eSIM Activation
- Supported on: iPhone XS and later, Android devices with eSIM support
- Process: Customer Portal → SIM Management → Switch to eSIM → Scan QR code
- Takes up to 30 minutes to activate

### SIM Lock / Blocking
- If customer reports phone stolen: block SIM immediately via Customer Portal → SIM Management → Block SIM
- Charges continue until SIM is blocked
- Once blocked, no calls/data can be made — service resumes when new SIM is activated

---

## Account Holder Change (Transfer of Ownership)

Required when account needs to transfer to a different person (marriage, death, business transfer):

1. Both parties must provide identity proof
2. Process cannot be done online — must visit a store or submit documents by post
3. Timeline: 5–10 business days

---

## Account Closure / Cancellation

### Process
1. Confirm the customer wants to cancel (retention offer may be appropriate — see below)
2. Check for minimum contract period (business accounts only)
3. Confirm final bill date and any outstanding balance
4. For mobile: offer to port number out — customer keeps their number
5. For broadband: arrange equipment return (router must be returned within 14 days)

### Retention Offers (Offer Before Processing Cancellation)
- If customer is leaving due to price: offer 10% loyalty discount for 6 months
- If customer is leaving due to service quality: escalate to Retention team before cancelling
- If customer is moving abroad: pause account for up to 6 months instead of cancelling

### Final Bill
- Final bill issued on next bill date after cancellation request
- Outstanding balance must be cleared before account is fully closed
- Equipment charges apply if router is not returned within 14 days: ₹2,500

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Account Management team if:
- Death of account holder (sensitive case protocol)
- Customer reports account taken over by someone else (account hijacking / fraud)
- Cancellation with disputed final bill

title: Mobile Network Issues — Signal, Calls, and Data
content:
# Mobile Network Issues — Signal, Calls, and Data

**Article ID:** ART007  
**Category:** Technical / Mobile  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article covers troubleshooting for mobile network issues including poor signal, dropped calls, mobile data not working, and SMS delivery failures.

---

## Step 1 — Quick Triage

Establish these facts before diagnosing:

1. Is the issue affecting **calls**, **data**, or **both**?
2. Is it location-specific or everywhere?
3. Does the issue persist after restarting the phone?
4. When did it start?
5. Has anything changed (new phone, SIM replacement, software update, moved home)?

---

## Scenario A — No Signal / Very Weak Signal

### Check First
- Is there a known **network outage** in the area? (Check internal outage tracker)
- Is the customer in a basement, rural area, or building with thick walls?

### Steps
1. Restart the phone
2. Manually search for network: Settings → Mobile Network → Network Operators → Select manually → Choose NexusNow → Set back to automatic
3. Check if SIM is seated properly (remove and reinsert)
4. If issue is building-specific → indoor coverage limitation (note in ticket, no fix possible without signal booster — available for purchase)
5. If issue is widespread in the area → log as network complaint, flag to Network team

### Signal Booster
- Available for purchase: ₹1,499 for small premises, ₹2,999 for large premises
- Not covered under standard plan — paid add-on

---

## Scenario B — Mobile Data Not Working

### Steps
1. Confirm data is not exhausted — check data balance in MySelf app
2. Check APN settings:
   - **APN:** nexusnow.internet  
   - **Username:** (leave blank)  
   - **Password:** (leave blank)  
   - **MCC:** 404, **MNC:** 20
3. Toggle mobile data off and on
4. Restart phone
5. If still not working → re-provision data service (internal tool → Account → Re-provision Mobile Data → Submit)
6. Allow 15 minutes for re-provisioning to take effect

### Data Exhausted
- Customer on Mobile Basic (5 GB): data throttled to 64 Kbps after limit
- Customer on Mobile Plus (20 GB): data throttled to 128 Kbps after limit  
- Customer on Mobile Max (100 GB): Fair Use Policy applies above 100 GB — throttled to 512 Kbps
- Top-up available: ₹99 for 2 GB (valid 30 days), ₹199 for 5 GB (valid 30 days)

---

## Scenario C — Dropped Calls / Poor Call Quality

1. Check for area network issues first
2. VoLTE: ensure VoLTE is enabled on the phone (required for HD calling)
3. Wi-Fi Calling: if signal is weak indoors, enable Wi-Fi Calling as alternative
   - Settings → Mobile Network → Wi-Fi Calling → On
4. If calls drop in a specific location repeatedly → log as coverage complaint
5. Persistent call quality issues → escalate to Network team with location coordinates

---

## Scenario D — SMS Not Sending / Receiving

1. Restart phone
2. Check message centre number: must be **+919900012345** (Settings → Messages → Advanced → SMS Service Centre)
3. Check if recipient's number is blocked
4. If group SMS failing: disable MMS (some handsets require data for group messages)
5. Persistent failures → re-provision SMS service (same process as data re-provisioning)

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Network Team if:
- Issue affects multiple customers in same area (area fault)
- Customer in critical location with no coverage (hospital, school, emergency services)
- Issue persists after 3 troubleshooting sessions
- Customer reports emergency call failure (999/112 calls)

---

## Coverage Complaints

If a customer's signal issue is due to coverage rather than a fault:
- Log a formal coverage complaint in the system
- Network team reviews within 5 business days
- Customer receives written response with coverage assessment
- No guarantee of improvement — be honest with customer

title: Speed Guarantee and Service Level Agreement (SLA) Policy
content:
# Speed Guarantee and Service Level Agreement (SLA) Policy

**Article ID:** ART008  
**Category:** Policies / SLA  
**Last Updated:** 2024-01-15  

---

## Overview

This article outlines our Speed Guarantee, service uptime SLAs, how customers can claim compensation, and what our obligations are when we fail to meet commitments.

---

## Speed Guarantee Policy

### Minimum Guaranteed Speeds

| Plan | Advertised Speed | Minimum Guaranteed (Wired) | Minimum Guaranteed (Wi-Fi) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fiber 100 | 100 Mbps | 50 Mbps | 30 Mbps |
| Fiber 500 | 500 Mbps | 250 Mbps | 150 Mbps |
| Fiber 1000 | 1000 Mbps | 500 Mbps | 300 Mbps |

**Wi-Fi speeds are not guaranteed** — they depend on router placement, interference, and device capability. Only wired Ethernet speeds are subject to the guarantee.

### How to Claim

1. Customer must run a speed test on a **wired connection** at [speedtest.nexusnow.com]
2. Test must be run at least 3 times across different times of day
3. All 3 tests must fall below the minimum guaranteed speed
4. Customer contacts support with test results (screenshots or test IDs)
5. Support logs a Speed Guarantee fault — engineer visit scheduled within 5 business days

### Remedies

| Duration Below Guarantee | Remedy |
|---|---|
| 1–5 days | Engineer visit + root cause fix |
| 6–10 days | 3 days bill credit + engineer visit |
| 11–20 days | 7 days bill credit + engineer visit |
| Over 20 days | Full month credit + engineer visit + option to exit contract without penalty |

---

## Service Uptime SLA

**Residential:** 99% uptime per calendar month  
**Business:** 99.5% uptime per calendar month (business accounts only)

**99% uptime** = maximum 7.2 hours downtime per month  
**99.5% uptime** = maximum 3.6 hours downtime per month

### Calculating Downtime Credit

Credit is calculated per day of confirmed outage:
- 1 day credit = (Monthly bill / 30)
- Applied automatically to next invoice when fault is marked resolved and outage duration confirmed

---

## Planned Maintenance

- Planned network maintenance: 24 hours advance notice via SMS and email
- Maintenance window: 2 AM – 6 AM local time (minimise customer impact)
- Planned maintenance downtime does **not** count toward SLA calculations
- Emergency maintenance: may occur without notice; does count toward SLA if over 4 hours

---

## What We Do Not Guarantee

- Wi-Fi speeds (as noted above)
- Speeds during customer-caused network congestion (e.g., 50 devices on one router)
- Service during events outside our control (natural disaster, power outage, civil emergency)
- Third-party service speed (Netflix, YouTube — speed test to nexusnow.com servers only)

---

## Ofcom / TRAI Regulatory Rights

Customers also have rights under TRAI regulations:
- Right to exit contract if service is consistently below guaranteed speed for 30 days
- Right to written explanation of any outage over 12 hours
- Right to formal complaint escalation if unresolved after 8 weeks

To file a formal regulatory complaint:
1. Contact support and request a **Formal Complaint Reference Number**
2. Allow 8 weeks for resolution
3. If unresolved: customer may refer to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)

---

## Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Service Quality team if:
- Customer threatens regulatory complaint / TDSAT referral
- Speed has been below guarantee for over 20 days
- Customer is a business account with uptime SLA breach
- Multiple customers in the same area report speed issues (potential infrastructure fault)
